His comments regarding the two party system are very ignorant, but I think also likely very common.

Imagine a state gets 10 representatives and is broken up evenly everywhere as 30% democrat, 27% republican, 20% libertarian, 20% socialist, 3% other. What parties should their representatives come from? Most anybody and everybody would say 3 democrats, 3 republicans, 2 libertarians, 2 socialists. That's proportional representation which we do not use (but the vast majority of the developed world does)! We use first past the post. What do we get in first past the post? 10 democrats!

How? We break the state up into 10 districts to awkwardly fit in first past the post. Now each district has their own little mini-election for a representative. We said the state was evenly broken up as well. District 1? Well it votes 30% democrat, 27% republican, and so on. So a democrat candidate wins. District 2, 3, 4...? Same story. You get 100% democrats even though they only received 30% of the vote.

Even in heads up elections, like for the presidency, first past the post sucks. Instead we could use an instant run-off system to mitigate the two party system. How does this work? It's easy. Instead of voting for one person. You vote for as many as you want in an order of priority. In the first round if somebody has more than 50% of all votes they win. If they don't then the person that received the lowest number of votes is knocked out and anybody who voted for them as #1 now goes to their #2 choice. We repeat until somebody gains more than 50% of the remaining vote. The benefit of this is that it removes third party spoiler effects. So imagine 36 people vote Trump, 39 vote Hillary, 9 vote Stein-Hillary, 16 vote Johnson-Trump.

  • Round 1: Trump - 36, Hillary - 39, 9 Stein-Hillary, 16 Johnson-Trump. Stein loses and is removed from the ballot. Since nobody has 50% yet we go to round 2.

  • Round 2: Trump - 36, Hillary 39 + 9, Johnson - 16. Johnson loses and is removed from the ballot. Since nobody has 50% yet we go to round 3.

  • Round 3: Trump - 36 + 16, Hillary 39 + 9. Trump has 52% of the vote and is declared the winner.

This enables a countless number of people to run without people having to worry about voting for somebody they don't really want as the president. It'd also prevent scenarios like today where Sanders has stated he won't run as a third party candidate because he doesn't want to give the election to Trump. People get to vote for who they want. Candidates can run without fear of their impact on the election. And in the end the person that wins is not the person that's least disliked but the person that would win a headsup election against any and every other candidate.

Our election system is a big part of our problems I think.
